evidence: The promoted entry says the store had "an 8 KB new generation" and then that the shallow pass was a no-op "because the new generation was already empty", which contradict each other. The agent declined the reviewer's "negligible" example and rewrote the causal clause to say that a shallow pass cannot touch the 72 MB old generation. That keeps both measurements and states the real reason.
guidance_note: When writing a changelog sentence that pairs a measured figure with an explanation, check that the explanation's wording ("empty", "zero") is consistent with the figure next to it before committing.

evidence: "Four candidate spellings... two matched, and the one that did NOT match" fails as arithmetic under any reading. The agent could not re-measure because the directories were pruned in #444. It removed the count instead of swapping in another unverifiable number, and kept the claim the argument depends on: the live mirror was unmatched.
guidance_note: When a changelog cites counts as evidence, check that the counts add up in the sentence itself at the time it is first written; that check needs no data.

narrative: A release-promotion PR that moved existing Unreleased prose under 0.10.0. The reviewer found two real internal inconsistencies in the promoted prose: "8 KB" next to "already empty", and a four/two/one count that does not add up. The agent accepted both premises and chose better fixes than the ones suggested: it rewrote the causal clause, and it dropped an unverifiable count rather than guessing a new one. Round 1 approved with nothing new.
guidance_observations: Both defects were in prose written in earlier PRs. That prose passed review there and was only caught when it was promoted, so an internal-consistency read of long changelog entries at authoring time would have avoided this round.
Saying exactly what was removed and why, instead of presenting the removal as a correction, was the right handling of evidence that can no longer be checked.

evidence: The reviewer says the collapse refusal lives in RankSet at memory/rank.go:81-128, outside the cited range 149-295. The packet does not include rank.go, so the line ranges cannot be checked. The thread was resolved with no reply, and the PR merged as its single commit, so nothing changed.
guidance_note: When one sentence makes two claims that come from different functions, give each claim its own citation instead of one trailing range.

evidence: The hunk shows the chapter citing internal/storage/specs.go twice: once for the semantic validation checks and once for decode-time rejection of unknown fields. That is consistent with the reviewer's claim that the first citation is misattributed. The packet does not contain specs.go or bulk.go to confirm it. Resolved silently with no fix.
guidance_note: When distilling an inventory into prose, carry each fact's citation from the inventory entry it came from instead of grouping a paragraph's files into one parenthetical.

evidence: The hunk shows "Topic is immutable through Apply entirely" placed right after the fieldChanges citation (memory/apply.go:253-270), so it reads as drawing on that range. The reviewer's alternative source (writeIssue at 320-331) is not in the packet. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Attach every factual sentence in a source-derived spec to its own citation; a sentence that only inherits the previous sentence's citation reads as misattributed.

evidence: The packet shows chapter 04 opening a "## The vendored Dolt driver" section, but it does not show chapter 03's section of the same name, so the claimed duplication cannot be confirmed. A total spec restating the same fact set in two chapters is a real drift risk if the claim holds. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Before assembling a multi-chapter spec, assign each subsystem to exactly one chapter and have the other chapters link to it instead of restating it.

evidence: The overview says "an append-only event history — one event per mutation". Chapter 02, visible in the F2 hunk, says "adding a comment records no history event". The PR contradicts itself, and the thread was resolved with no reply and no change.
guidance_note: When an overview states a universal invariant ("one X per Y"), search the detailed chapters for stated exceptions before writing it.

evidence: The overview credits the detached mirror process with push, receive, and compaction. Chapter 07, shown in the F17/F18 hunks, lists step 3 as spawning a background push, step 4 as an inline receive, and step 5 as the inline compaction backstop, all run by the foreground command. The overview contradicts its own source chapter. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Write the overview after the detailed chapters and check each attribution of work to a process against the chapter that specifies it.

evidence: The reviewer says model.go:556-562 is UnmarshalJSON container hydration, not the progress computation. The packet has neither model.go nor the inventory section, so this cannot be checked. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Cite the function that computes a derived value, not the place that happens to mark it as derived during decoding.

evidence: The hunk shows "36 methods total". The table the reviewer summed to 31 is not shown in the packet, so the count cannot be recomputed here, although the reviewer's per-interface arithmetic is specific. Resolved silently with the number unchanged.
guidance_note: Derive a stated total from the table next to it, or leave the total out, instead of writing a count separately.

evidence: The hunk shows "stacked at the top of the backlog" inside the contract-level vocabulary line, cited only to contract.go:154-177. Whether the contract text or conformance actually requires top placement cannot be confirmed from the packet. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: In a contract chapter, label reference-engine behavior as such and do not fold it into the contract vocabulary.

evidence: Chapter 04's transient-GC retry paragraph is visible (30 attempts, 50ms to 1s, two error shapes). Chapter 03's "Transient-retry classification" is not in the packet, so the near-verbatim duplication cannot be confirmed. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Assign each mechanism to one chapter before parallel drafting so that two chapter authors do not both describe it in full.

evidence: Chapter 04's "Mutation sequencing and commit rendering" is visible. Chapter 03's "One mutation, one commit" is not, so the duplication claim cannot be checked against the packet. This is the same pattern as F4 and F10. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Same move as F4/F10: assign ownership of each subsystem to one chapter before writing, and make the other chapters point to it.

evidence: The hunk shows withStampedMutation cited as commit_lock.go:122-177. The reviewer says 122-124 is the separate withMutation wrapper. commit_lock.go is not in the packet. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: When naming a specific function, cite that function's own line range, not the range of the wrapper that calls it.

evidence: The hunk shows the blanket statement "Each migration ships a down section with a documented loss contract". The per-version bullets the reviewer cites (v1 without loss-contract language) are below the visible hunk, so the internal inconsistency cannot be confirmed. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Check every "each" or "every" summary sentence against the per-item list that follows it in the same chapter.

evidence: The reviewer says doltcli.go:90-99 is runCommand rather than Run, and concedes that the described behavior is accurate end to end. The source is not in the packet. This is a minor citation-range issue at most. Resolved silently.

The hunk shows one trailing citation (syncfile.go:56-65) after a sentence describing both Read and HashFile, which supports the reviewer's point that Read has no citation. Whether 56-65 covers only HashFile cannot be checked from the packet. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Give each function described in a sentence its own citation.

evidence: The chapter lists `updated>=|>|<=|<|:<RFC3339>`. The reviewer says applyTimeTerm rejects `:` with "updated supports only >=, >, <=, <". query.go is not in the packet, but if that error string exists it settles the question. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: When documenting a grammar, list the forms the evaluator accepts, not the tokens the tokenizer recognizes.

evidence: The chapter presents "still running after 101s" as literal log text, but the format string uses %s with a time.Duration, and Go renders 101*time.Second as "1m41s". The same chapter writes the 24h threshold correctly as `24h0m0s`. Resolved silently, so a wrong grep string merged.
guidance_note: When quoting a runtime message produced by a format string, render each verb's argument the way the runtime formats it (Go Duration.String) instead of substituting the constant's source value.

evidence: The reviewer says the inventory has a ctx-canceled branch where teardownMirror records no push-outcome, and that the chapter drops this branch. The inventory is not in the packet. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: When condensing an inventory step that has conditional branches, keep every branch whose outcome differs; flattening them turns a conditional into an unconditional claim.

evidence: The hunk shows the quoted init refusal without a buildNote suffix. The reviewer's inventory citation for the `(<buildNote>)` suffix is not in the packet. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: When text is presented inside quote marks, copy the full format string; paraphrase without quote marks otherwise.

evidence: The hunk shows "any `--fix` ⇒ write, else read" with no parse-failure case. The reviewer's claim that a parse failure defaults to write comes from an inventory that is not in the packet. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: Carry fallback and error-path defaults from the inventory into the chapter, especially when they escalate privilege.

evidence: The same chapter requires the .zip entry to be named `lit.exe` (visible in the hunk), so a list that reads "no `/`, `\`, `..`, `.`" contradicts itself on a literal reading. The underlying rule is likely right and only ambiguously worded, which is why the premise is partly. Resolved silently.
guidance_note: When listing forbidden tokens, say whether each one is forbidden as an exact name or as a substring.

narrative: This PR added a 17k-line source-derived spec in one commit, and one review round raised 21 findings: citation misattributions, cross-chapter duplication, and several contradictions inside the PR itself. Every thread was resolved with no reply and no change, and the PR merged on its original commit. At least three findings can be confirmed from the packet: comments record no event (F5), the overview's mirror attribution (F6), and Go's Duration rendering (F17). Those are known-wrong statements merged into a document that presents itself as the specification.
guidance_observations: Resolving review threads without a plan reply or a fix skips the address-pr-reviews process completely; the dismissed review left no record of why each finding was dropped.

A spec drafted by parallel per-chapter passes needs a cross-chapter consistency pass (shared invariants, ownership of each subsystem) before review; most of the findings come from chapters disagreeing with or duplicating each other.
A PR this large cannot be checked by the auditor from the packet, and that is a reason to answer each thread explicitly instead of resolving it in bulk.

evidence: The doc defines epic state as "computed from its children" and never says what happens with zero children, which is a real gap. The agent cited all_of.go:17-27, where Closed requires progress.Total > 0, and added "(an epic with no children counts as open)".
guidance_note: When describing a derived value in prose, state the empty-input case alongside the rule.

evidence: Lanes are introduced only as "Inside an epic", while claims are defined per lane, so standalone tickets looked unprotected. The agent cited model.LaneOf, which makes a parentless ticket a lane of one, and the doc now says so. The mechanism was fine; the doc had left it out.
guidance_note: When a feature overview defines a mechanism in terms of a concept scoped to a subset ("inside an epic"), state how items outside that subset are handled.

evidence: "Records the taker as its assignee" left the identity undefined, next to a privacy claim and a "human-readable owner string". The agent identified the acting identity (claude_<session-id>, else --assignee, else blank), which matches the #449 overview's "acting identity defaults to claude_<session-id>", and named it in the doc.
guidance_note: When a doc introduces two identity concepts, state which identity each operation writes.

evidence: Both "ahead of everything else" (focus) and "before anything else" (epic continuation) were written as absolute, and they can conflict. The agent cited the routing order in next_route.go, where own held lanes come before the global pool where focus applies, and scoped both sentences.
guidance_note: Use "ahead of everything else" for at most one mechanism; when two mechanisms both reorder work, state their precedence.

evidence: The token is printed in the refusal with the exact re-invocation. The #449 chapter text ("Do not self-approve; approval asserted without the owner's explicit instruction is a false claim") shows the owner requirement is prose, not a mechanism, so "the tool enforces that" overclaimed. The agent rewrote it as a mechanism plus a stated norm.
guidance_note: Describe a safety property only as strongly as its mechanism enforces it; when the guarantee depends on the reader following instructions, call it a norm.

evidence: The doc said a session ID "becomes its acting identity" right after saying claims key on the checkout token, and never stated how the two layer, so a new session might look like a different holder. The agent cited claims keyed on the stream token (derive.go) and the session ID recorded separately as the actor, and made the layering explicit.
guidance_note: When a doc introduces two identity concepts, state which identity each operation writes.

evidence: The merge paragraph claims field-by-field rules but omits assignee and retention, both of which the doc introduces earlier. The agent cited the existing rules in resolve.go and retention.go and added them.
guidance_note: When a paragraph claims to cover all fields, check it against the field list given earlier in the same doc.

narrative: This is a standalone feature-overview doc. Round 0 found seven omissions and overclaims: the empty-epic case, standalone lanes, the assignee identity, focus vs epic precedence, an enforced-human-gate overclaim, session vs checkout identity, and missing merge rules. The agent accepted each one after checking source, cited file:line in its plans, and fixed all seven in one commit. Round 1 approved with nothing new.
guidance_observations: Every finding was a completeness or overclaim gap in prose. A pre-review pass that checks each absolute claim ("ahead of everything", "the tool enforces", "field by field") against the mechanism would have caught most of them.
Verifying each premise in source before accepting, and citing the line in the plan, is the behavior #449 skipped completely.

evidence: `pinned := strings.TrimSpace(*to) != ""` sends an explicit `--to ""` to the latest-release path, which is an unrequested action that used to be a validation error. The fix commit 36f1f8d switched to `fs.Changed("to")` and added TestRunUpgradeExplicitEmptyToIsRejected covering both empty and whitespace values.
guidance_note: When turning a required flag into an optional one with a default, distinguish omitted from explicitly empty using the flag set's Changed bit, so a broken shell expansion still fails.

evidence: The doc said "installs a newer lit binary", but a pinned --to has no ordering check, only the schema-coverage refusal. The reviewer offered two options. The agent took the doc fix ("not necessarily a newer one") and explained why schema coverage is the deliberate refusal boundary. 36f1f8d shows the reworded doc.
guidance_note: When writing a command's reference entry, use only words ("newer") that some check in the code actually enforces.

evidence: The comment documented a dev-build corner case (unstamped Version) that no test exercised. In 36f1f8d the agent added TestRunUpgradeBareDevBuildAlwaysInstalls and also made the guard typed (`!current.IsDev`) instead of relying on string inequality.
guidance_note: When a code comment explains why a corner case is safe, either add a test that exercises the corner case or make the safety structural.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. Both adjacent sentences were already in the round-0 text: "(and, at the running version, doubles as a reinstall...)" and the unscoped "Already being on the latest release is a no-op". 36f1f8d reworded the --to clause for F2 but did not create the ambiguity. The no-op is gated on !pinned, so the unscoped sentence misleads; fixed in c120b45.
guidance_note: When a behavior applies to only one invocation form, scope the doc sentence to that form, matching the gate in the code (`!pinned`).

evidence: The flag on c120b45 (a doc-only scoping fix) is a false positive. The equality guard `target.Manifest.Version == current.Version` dates from round 0, and the backward-move gap is in the original design. GitHub's releases/latest returns the most recently created release, so an older backport can be "latest". 747b78b switched to an ordering check with a test.
guidance_note: When a default target comes from an external "latest" feed, check what the feed's ordering actually means (creation time vs version) before writing a guard that assumes latest is newest.

evidence: 747b78b introduced `semver.Compare("v"+current.Version, tag) >= 0`. x/mod/semver sorts any invalid version below a valid one, and acceptTag only enforces `^v[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$` (quoted in the #449 platform chapter). So a tag like "vnightly" now makes bare upgrade a no-op, where the old equality guard would have installed it. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted and gated on semver.IsValid in 16bb888.
guidance_note: When replacing an equality check with a library ordering check, read the library's contract for invalid operands and check whether the upstream validator admits them before relying on the comparison.

evidence: 747b78b changed the guard from equality to at-or-ahead but touched only upgrade.go and the test. cli-reference ("already on the latest release") and the CHANGELOG clause still described equality. Fixed in 16bb888.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a predicate's semantics, grep the docs and changelog for prose describing the old predicate and update them in the same commit.

evidence: This duplicates F7 on the same line: the doc and changelog say "on the latest" while 747b78b's guard is `>= 0`. The agent identified it as a duplicate and applied the same 16bb888 change.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a predicate's semantics, grep the docs and changelog for prose describing the old predicate and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. "The installed binary migrates the workspace forward on its next run" was already in the round-0 doc text, and 747b78b did not touch docs. The command's own success message says "if it trails", so the doc overclaimed. Fixed in 16bb888.
guidance_note: When a command already prints a qualified message, copy that qualification into its reference doc instead of restating the behavior unconditionally.

narrative: This PR made bare `lit upgrade` resolve the latest release. Round 0's three findings were real and fixed well. Rounds 1 and 2 surfaced gaps that were already in the original text and design: an unscoped doc no-op, and a feed-latest backward move. The F5 fix replaced equality with semver.Compare. It introduced a regression for non-strict feed tags (F6) and left the docs describing equality (F7/F8), and together these produced most of round 3 and made round 4 necessary. Every agent response was a correct accept.
guidance_observations: The F5 fix changed the meaning of a predicate without touching the doc and changelog that describe it, and adopted a library comparator without checking its invalid-input behavior against the validator upstream. Both misses were visible in one read of the surrounding code.

Several ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags here (F4, F5, F9) are pre-existing text and logic that the reviewer only reached on later passes. The real cost was a reviewer converging slowly on the original diff, not fix churn.

Five rounds for a feature with a narrow surface suggests the original PR would have benefited from enumerating the no-op guard's inputs (dev build, equal, ahead, unorderable tag) before the first review.
